A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-ICM research. All 27 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support matching text, equations, figures and tables across the revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original CLIP-ICM classification experiments on five DomainBed datasets, augmentation and hyperparameter ablations, and domain-prompt experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original DomainBed experiments and adds results for text-based interventions, unseen-class evaluation, ImageNet distribution shifts and intervention-count ablations.

M1.justification: V2 estimates its projection from original and augmented image embeddings. V3 Section 6 and Appendix H add GPT-4o-generated captions and intervened descriptions, text-only training, and joint training with image-image, text-text and cross-modal pairs. Algorithm 1 consequently uses both encoders. This substantially extends the procedure beyond renaming the projection matrix.

E1.justification: All five original DomainBed datasets remain; PACS and Office-Home were already evaluated in v2's appendix. V3 adds scenarios combining domain shift with previously unseen classes on Office-Home, DomainNet and Terra Incognita. Appendix J also adds ImageNet training and evaluation on ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds evaluated comparisons with MIRO, CoOp, CoCoOp and CLIP-Adapter. DPL already appeared in v2 Table 10; its comparison now also covers DomainNet. Most earlier comparators remain in Appendix O, but the SIG versus CLIP-ICM comparison on DomainNet with ResNet101 in v2 Table 9 is removed.

E3.justification: V3 introduces base-class-only training followed by separate base/new/total evaluation, target-domain linear-probe controls, and ImageNet-to-variant transfer evaluation. Its text-intervention experiments use all images from smaller datasets but a 20% subset for DomainNet and ImageNet. The reported augmentation list also adds RandomRotation; this does not establish that retained image-only experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 systematically compares image-only, text-only and joint interventions, testing the contribution and complementarity of the new component. Appendix M.4 and Figure 6(d) add sensitivity analysis over intervention counts. The three earlier augmentation, regularization and subspace-dimension plots are retained as Figure 6(a-c), and the domain-prompt analysis remains.

E5.justification: V3 Table 2 newly supplies uncertainty for previously reported dataset averages: for example, CLIP linear-probe VLCS accuracy changes from a point estimate of 78.7 to 78.7 ± 0.2. Both versions already report per-domain uncertainties. Neither specifies the repeated-run count or clearly defines the ± quantities, so additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Many earlier results survive under the image-only asterisk, while substantial text-only, joint, unseen-class and ImageNet result blocks are added. For example, Terra Incognita linear-probe accuracy of 64.3 is retained for image-only CLIP-ICM, while the new joint variant reports 66.5 in v3 Table 12. Some new entries are inconsistent: v3 Table 11 prints 87.1 for joint Office-Home domain scores averaging 84.6.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3's empirical-risk, Rademacher-complexity and divergence condition is replaced by Theorem 5.6's mutual-information condition and a new Appendix G proof. Identifiability assumptions change to Condition 5.2's D+1 text pairs, and the coordinate-identification theorem becomes a projection constraint on interventional pairs. Proposition 5.1 also reformulates the causal result as changing versus invariant interventional mechanisms.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift the central problem from CLIP's poor cross-domain performance to degradation after fine-tuning, particularly loss of unseen-class recognition. The contributions expand to an image-or-text intervention framework and preservation of zero-shot capability during adaptation. Conditional invariant prediction remains the central underlying idea.

C2.justification: New Appendix B explains how different fine-tuning strategies can misalign embeddings and overfit base classes. V3 interprets joint image/text results as complementary and discusses diminishing returns from additional intervention pairs. It also removes v2's explicit limitation that evaluation covers only classification tasks, although the reported evaluations remain classification-based.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix H adds caption/intervention prompts, GPT-4o identification, embedding-pair construction, sampling fractions, computational-cost analysis and a reported data-collection cost of $162.79. However, v2's linear-probe details—Scikit-learn, 1000 epochs and an L1 penalty of 1e-4—and its statement that supplementary code is provided disappear. The GPU and under-one-hour training statement remain.

R1.justification: V3 expands positioning around CLIP adaptation and synthetic/interventional data generation, adding MIRO, ImageNet-shift and generative-data references. It removes the dedicated Wald et al. calibration comparison and several causal-representation references. Appendix L substantively rewrites the DPL comparison as test-time adaptation versus domain generalization and the Kügelgen comparison around linear versus nonlinear identification.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial theoretical/methodological prose are rewritten. Problem setting and motivation become separate sections, identifiability analysis moves before OOD-risk analysis, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. These are extensive narrative and structural changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is redrawn with an invariant-projection panel; new figures present the complete pipeline, fine-tuning strategies and caption interventions. Results are reorganized into main-text summaries and expanded appendix tables. The original ablation plots are rearranged and supplemented with a fourth panel, while notation tables become lists.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the motivation with target-domain controls and adds useful unseen-class tests, modality ablations and intervention-generation details. However, it introduces conflicting central results: Table 11 reports 87.1 for scores averaging 84.6, whereas v2 Table 8 reports those scores consistently. Tables 2 and 12 also disagree on text-only Terra Incognita results, and earlier linear-probe settings disappear. The rewritten OOD proof still makes an unsupported bound-to-risk inference in Appendix G, Equations 39-40. These substantive gains and reliability losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
